newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end up on forestry, utilities.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end up on forestry, utilities.

text.p: Swedish share prices ended slightly higher on Tuesday in dull trade, boosted by power companies and the forestry sector.
The Stockholm general index rose 0.10 percent to 2,531.29 after shares worth 3.8 billion crowns changed hands.
Brokers said there was nothing to spark the bourse's imagination with no company results, interest rates unchanged and Wall Street opening hesitantly.
"This has been a dull day. Everyone is waiting for the results from the Federal Reserve meeting (that starts at 1930 GMT)," one broker said.
"The only really positive thing is the dollar that is continuing to be strong."
Power companies continued to rise in the wake of government plans, announced on Monday, to begin phasing out Sweden's nuclear programme. Electricity prices could rise, brokers say.
Sydkraft closed 6.5 crowns higher at 146. Graninge climbed four to 127 crowns followed by Gullspang that rose six to 122 crowns.
The forestry sector benefited from the stronger dollar, rising 1.91 percent. AssiDoman closed 3.5 higher at 181.5 and Stora was 2.50 higher at 94 crowns.
The day's winner was television company TV4 that rose seven to 169 crowns after media group Tidnings AB Marieberg bought 16.7 percent of capital. Marieberg shares slipped three to 215 crowns.

The bank sector calmed down after Monday's news that a merger between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken would not proceed. S-E-Banken shares fell 1.5 crowns to 66 crowns and Nordbanken shares edged up 0.5 crown to 228.
